segments.title: Chương 235: 0236【Mục đích vẫn là kiếm tiền từ nhạc chuông】
segments.content:
"Fan Bingbing's agent just called."

"What's it about?"

"In view of the numerous online rumors questioning if she's had plastic surgery, she'll be going to a hospital after this year's Gaokao to get an official evaluation, and she'll have an authoritative notary office present to certify it."

"She's giving this news to us?"

"The news rights have already been given to Sina Entertainment. Sina will send people to film the entire process. The day after Sina Entertainment's report, she will upload the photos and the notarized certificate to Hainei and her Sina blog. Oh, and she wants to buy the number one spot on Hainei's trending list for that day."

"This is a great way to attract attention!"

June had just begun, and Fan Ye was already planning a stunt.

This was good news for Hainei. Besides being Super Girl's official platform, a celebrity was finally taking the initiative to buy a spot on the trending list.

Of course, when it came to stunts, no one could beat 'Big Mouth' Song.

The one who claimed Liu Tianxian was a transsexual, making such a fuss that the matter ended up on "Legal Report."

'Big Mouth' Song had also registered an account on Hainei, and the first article he posted was: "I have submitted a ten-thousand-word letter, 'Save the Children—A Letter to the State Administration of Radio, Film, and Television,' urging them to ban Mango TV from holding the Super Girl competition. Super Girl misleads people and makes a fortune, luring so many children down the wrong path. They've created a fictitious idol, Li Yuchun, blatantly providing poisonous spiritual food to children..."

After this thing was published, 'Big Mouth' Song's Hainei account gained over 30,000 followers in a single day.

A bunch of people cursed him out.

And another bunch defended him.

The two sides started fighting directly in the comments section.

Then, 'Big Mouth' Song exposed the inside story of Huang Shengyi's contract termination with Stephen Chow. He made it sound so convincing, claiming Huang Shengyi had told him personally, because he had played her love interest last year. In a film he had invested in himself...

Now, whenever Chen Guiliang logged into Hainei, the first thing he did was check if 'Big Mouth' Song had cooked up any new stunts.

The man was just too damn bizarre.

After a certain major case was cracked, 'Big Mouth' Song had specifically gone to a judicial auction to buy the Porsche of one of the criminals, then publicly declared he was going to give it to the sweet-voiced pop queen with the surname Yang. From then on, he had embarked on a path of pulling stunts.

Chen Guiliang clicked on 'Big Mouth' Song's personal homepage and immediately saw his new post: "I've invested in a new film, and the female lead has been confirmed to be Li Xiaolu. We'll also be inviting the famous actress Zhang Yu to participate..."

Zhang Yu was the one who had exposed herself for sleeping with over 30 directors.

After reading the article, Chen Guiliang had a premonition that 'Big Mouth' Song's post today was just a small prelude to his new stunt.

"Senior, I'm about to enter the exam hall," Tao Xue texted.

Chen Guiliang replied: "Good luck. May you succeed on your first try!"

"Mm!"

Tao Xue took a deep breath and handed her phone to her brother.

What she didn't know was that she was about to face the most absurd Gaokao in Longdu's history. Not only did the entire city fail to produce a single student admitted to Tsinghua or Peking University, but the acceptance rate for undergraduate programs also plummeted.

And it was only this particular year, affecting every high school in the city.

Tao Chenggang watched his sister walk into the exam hall. Standing outside with nothing to do, he was so bored he simply called Chen Guiliang. "Shi Yuzhu is being too unreasonable. A promotional team of over 2000 people, going to internet cafes all over the country to partner with them. It's only been a little over a month, and I hear they've already set up more than 100 offices nationwide."

"Let's take it slow," Chen Guiliang could only console him.

Tao Chenggang grumbled, "I've been working on this for over half a year, and he surpassed my game's concurrent player count in just one month. But 'Zhengtu' has a terrible reputation now. It's 'Zhengtu' everywhere, online and offline, and it's already drawing a lot of resentment from netizens."

"How much revenue did 'Power and Dominion' make last month?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Tao Chenggang laughed. "Revenue was over 28 million, with a net profit exceeding 13 million. I'm also expanding my promotional team, planning to cover all the second and third-tier cities."

Chen Guiliang sighed to himself. Compared to these cash-grab games, "Sanguosha" really didn't make much money.

Tao Chenggang said, "There's a player called Zhongyuan Baotu. We speculate his family elders are from Jiangsu or Zhejiang and operate coal mines in Shanxi Province. Whenever he logs on, he recharges at least twenty thousand, sometimes fifty thousand. And he doesn't even play the national wars much, he just spends all that money for fun. The game specially added several new gift items for him, because he wants to buy gifts for the girls in the game."

"The coal bosses have money to burn, let's help them spend some," Chen Guiliang joked.

Tao Chenggang said, "If I weren't in the gaming industry, I'd find it hard to imagine people like this exist in real life. They literally throw money around for fun. The game created a special gift leaderboard for him, to see which player receives the most gifts."

"Haha, that's a pretty good leaderboard," Chen Guiliang couldn't help but laugh, reminded of live-streaming PK battles for gifts.

The landline rang, and Chen Guiliang pressed the speakerphone button.

His secretary, Hu Yuexia, said, "Boss, a Mr. Wang Hao is here to see you."

"Please show him in."

Chen Guiliang then spoke into his phone, "I have to go."

"Talk later."

"Okay, bye."

Wang Hao walked into the office and shook his hand with a smile. "Mr. Chen, I've heard so much about you."

"Not at all, not at all. Please, have a seat," Chen Guiliang said.

Wang Hao was direct, getting straight to the point. "Let me share my idea. I plan to completely overhaul that music forum. I still insist on doing paid music."

"Do you have that many copyrights?" Chen Guiliang said, "I know someone who ran a legal, paid music site. He shut it down last year and went back to his research institute to be a researcher."

Wang Hao said, "My ideal music website is one where users pay to download. The website then pays copyright fees to the record companies based on the number of downloads. Sigh, the record companies aren't willing to go for a slow and steady stream of income. They all just sell the copyrights in a one-time deal."

"Tell me the specifics of how you plan to operate," Chen Guiliang said.

Wang Hao explained in detail, "Users will upload music files, and the website will conduct a strict review. We will absolutely not use web crawlers or hotlinking. The minimum quality for user-uploaded songs will be 320kbps, far superior to the currently popular 128kbps."

"The song information must include the artist, album, track number, genre, year, language, and songwriter. If there's a record label, it must be indicated. Vague information like 'Unknown Artist' or 'Various Artists' will not be allowed. If a user uploads a whole album, the track order must be correct."

"I want to create a Wikipedia for the music world!"

"Users who upload high-quality resources or participate in reviewing resources can earn points. To download songs, you must use points. Points can be obtained by topping up with RMB."

The more Chen Guiliang listened, the more it felt off. This kind of community-operated model, how was it so similar to VeryCD?

Wang Hao continued, "If there are infringing songs and the copyright holder comes knocking, I'll negotiate a partnership with them. That is, we'll pay them a share of the copyright fees based on download counts. If we really can't reach an agreement, then we'll have no choice but to take it down."

In other words, it would still operate through infringement.

But it would be very conscientious infringement, not stealing others' copyrights, and certainly not using them to operate ringback tones. And as long as the copyright holders agreed, they were even willing to give them a share of the fees based on download counts.

"Why did you leave Alibaba?" Chen Guiliang was quite curious.

Wang Hao said, "I was in a band in college. In '99, I set up an underground music website. Before Taobao was even launched, I'd already built a website to sell musical instruments. Business was pretty good."

"And I'm not some 'Alibaba technical director' like the rumors say. I'm just too proactive when I write code. After finishing my own tasks, I like to help others refactor their code. My boss asked me to develop the TrustPass feature, and I ended up refactoring everyone else's front end while I was at it. The UseCase systems for both Alibaba and Taobao were also built by me, and they're still in use today."

He said these things with a hint of pride, while also showcasing his abilities to Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang asked, "How much are you looking to sell that music forum for?"

"It's not worth much," Wang Hao said. "The music site I built in '99 had tens of thousands of users by '01, and I still shut it down just like that. What's valuable is me. Everyone in the Hangzhou music scene knows me. My 100,000 users are all enthusiasts, and I have a very good relationship with them."

Chen Guiliang reminded him, "You're taking the 'small and beautiful' route. Once anything gets big, commercialization is an inevitable path."
